author: copilot
body:
IO file documentation was missing procedures that read files via compound variable parameters. For example, `hru.con` only listed `gwflow_read` but not `hyd_read_connect`, even though the latter reads from the same file when called as `hyd_read_connect(in_con%hru_con, ...)`.

## Changes

**ford/fortran_project.py (lines 1678-1698)**
- Enhanced call-site resolution to resolve compound variable names (e.g., `in_con%hru_con`) to their actual filename values
- When a parameter contains `%`, split into variable and component parts, look up the variable's type in `var_to_type_map`, then construct and resolve the full `typename%component` key in `type_defaults_map`

**test/test_example.py**
- Added "I/O" to expected navigation links to account for IO file tracking feature

## Example

Before: `in_con%hru_con` couldn't be resolved because `type_defaults_map` only contains keys like `input_con%hru_con` (type name, not variable name).

After:
```python
# Split compound name
var_name = "in_con"  # from in_con%hru_con
component = "hru_con"

# Look up variable's type
type_name = var_to_type_map[var_name]  # "input_con"

# Resolve to filename
filename = type_defaults_map[f"{type_name}%{component}"]  # "hru.con"
```

This enables FORD to correctly link IO operations in parameterized procedures to their actual files.

In the derive macro, we currently determine whether a struct qualifies for zero-copy by checking that the `repr` is `C` or `transparent` and all its fields are also `zero_copy: true`.

This PR adds an additional qualification: the struct's serialized size must equal its in-memory size; i.e., it has no padding. The importance of this is twofold:
1. Bincode never serializes padding, so we must enforce this to uphold our default bincode-compatible promise.
2. Soundness; implementations are free to serialize zero-copy types using their direct in-memory representation. `SchemaRead` implementations may use the `size` field of `TypeMeta` to read a fixed number of bytes and memcpy those bytes directly into the destination. If `T::TypeMeta::Static {size} != size_of::<T>()` (the serialized size != the in-memory size) that memcpy will not fully initialize the type.

This additional check solves both of these issues.

author: ishandhanani
body:
## Problem

When running `compile_deep_gemm` with `SGLANG_CUTEDSL_MOE_NVFP4_DISPATCH=1`, the process fails with an assertion error:

```python
AssertionError at modelopt_quant.py:1454
assert torch.all(w13_input_scale == w13_input_scale[0])
```

This occurs because:
- `compile_deep_gemm` uses `load_format="dummy"` to speed up compilation
- Dummy weight initialization assigns random values to quantization scales
- Each expert gets a different random `w13_input_scale` value
- The NVFP4 dispatch path requires uniform scales across all experts

Notably, this assertion does not fail during normal `launch_server` because real checkpoints have properly initialized scales.

## Solution

This PR modifies the assertion to handle dummy weights gracefully:

- Detects when running in DeepGEMM precompile stage via `SGLANG_IN_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE_STAGE`
- If scales differ during precompile, logs a warning and uses the first expert's scale for all experts
- For normal inference with real checkpoints, preserves the original strict behavior with a more informative error message
- The scale values don't affect kernel compilation (only shapes/dtypes matter), so using a uniform dummy value is safe

## Testing [WIP]

- Existing functionality preserved: real checkpoints with uniform scales continue to work
- Enables `compile_deep_gemm` to run with `SGLANG_CUTEDSL_MOE_NVFP4_DISPATCH=1`
- Better error messages help users diagnose scale mismatch issues

## Description

Proxies FastAPI documentation endpoints (`/docs`, `/redoc`, `/openapi.json`) through the frontend nginx server, making them accessible via HTTPS at `/api/docs`, `/api/redoc`, and `/api/openapi.json`.

## Motivation & Context

Previously, API documentation required direct access to the backend server on port 8080, bypassing the frontend's TLS termination. This created an inconsistent access pattern and exposed the backend port unnecessarily.

## Implementation Details

**Nginx configuration changes:**
- Added exact-match location blocks (`location =`) to both `nginx.conf` and `nginx-ssl.conf.template`
- Proxies documentation paths with standard proxy headers for proper request forwarding
- Uses exact matching to avoid conflicts with existing `/api/` prefix routes

```nginx
location = /api/docs {
    proxy_pass http://api_upstream/docs;
    proxy_set_header Host $host;
    proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
    proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
}
```

**Documentation additions:**
- `DOCS_ACCESS.md`: Complete guide with architecture diagram, deployment modes, authentication patterns, and security considerations
- Updated `README.md` and `QUICKSTART.md` with new access URLs
- Created `test-docs-access.sh` for endpoint validation

**Backward compatibility:**
- Direct server access (`http://localhost:8080/docs`) remains functional

**Description of changes:**

This PR adds AMD GPU DKMS driver support for Bottlerocket kernel 6.12, enabling users to run newer AMD GPU hardware with the latest out-of-tree drivers. It also includes systemd services to ensure proper driver initialization before dependent services start.

**Dependencies**

⚠️ Blocked by: https://github.com/bottlerocket-os/bottlerocket-kernel-kit/pull/325

This PR requires AMD GPU firmware support to be merged first. The firmware files are necessary for the AMD GPU drivers to initialize properly. 

**Changes**

1. Disable In-Tree AMD GPU Driver

Why: Out-of-tree DKMS drivers typically support newer GPU hardware faster than in-tree drivers and receive updates independently of kernel releases.

What changed:
 - Disabled CONFIG_DRM_AMDGPU in both x86_64 and aarch64 kernel configs
 - Updated kernel patch 1006 to explicitly select DRM helper modules (DRM_DISPLAY_HDCP_HELPER and DRM_DISPLAY_HDMI_HELPER) that were previously bundled with the in-tree driver but are required as standalone modules for DKMS builds
 - Eliminates driver conflicts by ensuring exclusive hardware access

2. Add AMD GPU DKMS Kernel Module

What: New kmod-6.12-amdgpu package that builds AMD GPU drivers from upstream DKMS source.

Key features:
  - Sources drivers from AMD's official DKMS repository (version 30.20)
  - Dynamic kernel version detection - automatically adapts to kernel updates without hardcoded dependencies
  - Full cross-compilation support integrated with Bottlerocket's build toolchain
  - GPG signature verification of upstream driver packages
  - Includes all required kernel modules: amdgpu, amdkcl, amdttm, amddrm_*, amd-sched, amdxcp

- Ensures compatibility with latest Turso features

### 2. Batch Operations
- `execute_batch`: Execute multiple statements sequentially
- `execute_transactional_batch`: Execute statements atomically (all-or-nothing)
- Reduces network roundtrips for bulk operations
- Auto-sync support for remote replica mode

### 3. Prepared Statements
- `prepare()`: Compile SQL statements once, reuse multiple times
- `query_stmt()`: Execute SELECT queries with prepared statements
- `execute_stmt()`: Execute INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE with prepared statements
- `close_stmt()`: Clean up prepared statement resources
- Significant performance improvement for repeated queries

## Priority 2 - Production-Ready Features

### 4. Transaction Behaviors
- DEFERRED: Default, lock acquired on first write
- IMMEDIATE: Lock acquired immediately for write transactions
- EXCLUSIVE: Exclusive lock, blocks all readers
- READ_ONLY: Read-only transactions
- Exposed via `begin(state, behavior: :immediate)` API

### 5. Metadata Methods
- `last_insert_rowid()`: Get rowid of last inserted row
- `changes()`: Get number of rows affected by last operation
- `total_changes()`: Get total changes since connection opened
- `is_autocommit()`: Check if in autocommit mode

None - All changes are backward compatible. Existing code continues to work.

body:
This reverts commit 2b848cca366fbd3cfd0cb7281078980b202f33d5.

The commit's assumption that `copyUIDGID=true` means that UID/GID from the tar should be preserved does not seem to be true. Opposite is true: if `copyUIDGUID=true` the main UID/GID of the container is used. I tested this on `moby`.

Also brief look at the source code seems to confirm this:
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/16880e9e1ba21593215b40241d62c043410e0ae7/daemon/archive_unix.go#L136-L144
https://github.com/moby/moby/blob/16880e9e1ba21593215b40241d62c043410e0ae7/daemon/archive_tarcopyoptions_unix.go#L22-L30

Yes it's quite contra-intuitive but it does behave that way.

See this issue opened since 2017 https://github.com/moby/moby/issues/34096

>Now, docker cp hostfile container:containerpath will copy a file from the host to the container but preserving the original uid/gid (with the respective mapping to the container). docker cp -a hostfile container:containerpath (as defined in the documentation) is meant to "copy all uid/gid information" but it is in fact setting the uid and gid to the main user inside the container.

Also apparently there was a PR to fix this https://github.com/moby/moby/pull/34099 but is has newer been merged.

And another bug report  https://github.com/docker/docs/issues/17533 that suggest to change in documentation instead of the behaviour.

Added an Amazon-style location selector so customers always see products and delivery options that match where they live.

What this feature does

 Detects your location automatically using GPS (with your permission)

 Allows manual pincode entry if you prefer to type it yourself

 Looks up city and state from the pincode so you don’t have to

 Keeps the selected location in sync between the header and product detail pages

 Remembers your location using localStorage, even if you refresh or open a new tab

How it works technically

Uses OpenStreetMap Nominatim for reverse geocoding (GPS → city/state)

Uses the India Post API to fetch details from a pincode

Uses custom browser events + localStorage so the header and product detail page always show the same location

Location data persists across page reloads and browser tabs

LocationModal.tsx – The popup/modal where users can detect or enter their location

locationUtils.ts – Helper functions for GPS, geocoding, and pincode lookups
